Section 1

1. What This Website Is & Who It Is For

Verdant Hearth is a production-grade, multi-page restaurant and hospitality website template built on Astro 6, TypeScript (strict mode), and Tailwind CSS 4. It was designed from the ground up to solve the most painful challenges faced by independent fine-dining restaurants, farm-to-table bistros, wood-fired hearth eateries, artisanal bakeries, botanical cocktail bars, and the agencies or freelancers building sites for them.

Why Restaurants Choose It

  • ✦ Blazing Fast: Static HTML output with zero client JavaScript runtime by default.
  • ✦ High Conversion: Sticky category filtering and instant frictionless online reservations.
  • ✦ Flawless Mobile: Engineered for iPhone & Android ergonomics with thumb-friendly controls.
  • ✦ Full SEO & Schema: Structured Schema.org Restaurant JSON-LD, OpenGraph, and auto sitemap.
  • ✦ Zero Font Requests: Self-hosted OFL typography—no external Google Fonts network calls.

How It Benefits the Business

  • ✦ More Direct Bookings: Reduces reliance on third-party portals charging per-cover fees.
  • ✦ Effortless Menu Updates: Change dishes in one typed file or connect any headless CMS.
  • ✦ Virtually Free Hosting: Deploys effortlessly to free-tier edge CDNs (Vercel, Netlify, Cloudflare).
  • ✦ 100% Commercial Safety: Verified copyright-free photography and custom SVG staff avatars.
Section 2

2. How to Run It (Local PC & Git Deployment)

Two straightforward paths exist to install and run the template: locally on your development workstation or directly deployed from a GitHub repository to edge platforms.

Path A: Local PC (macOS, Windows, Linux)

# 1. Requirements: Node.js 18.17+ or 20+ (Check with: node -v)
# 2. Extract or open directory
cd nexora

# 3. Install dependencies
npm install

# 4. Start local development server
npm run dev
# The website will launch at http://localhost:4321

# 5. Type-check & build production static assets
npm run build

# 6. Preview the production build locally
npm run preview

Path B: Git & Edge Hosting (Vercel / Netlify)

# 1. Clone repository from GitHub
git clone https://github.com/your-username/verdant-hearth-restaurant.git
cd verdant-hearth-restaurant

# 2. Install and verify build
npm install
npm run build

# 3. One-Click Deploy to Vercel or Netlify
# Push repository to GitHub, link repository in Vercel or Netlify dashboard.
# Build command: npm run build
# Output directory: dist
# Environment variable: PUBLIC_API_BASE_URL (Optional, leave blank for demo mode)

Section 4

4. API Architecture & Section Mapping Table

Verdant Hearth uses a transparent two-tier data architecture:

  • 1. Without API (Demo Mode): If PUBLIC_API_BASE_URL is omitted, all queries and form submissions fall back gracefully to local typed mock data in src/data/restaurant.ts.
  • 2. With API Connected: Once PUBLIC_API_BASE_URL is defined, src/lib/data.ts and src/lib/api.ts route requests to your live REST backend.
  • 3. Static Build vs. Live Submissions: Content like menu dishes, artisan profiles, and stories are rendered at static build time. When menu data changes in your backend database, trigger a webhook rebuild on your host (e.g., Vercel Deploy Hook). Interactive forms (Reservations, Contact, Newsletter) submit live POST requests via client fetch directly to your API.

Connecting Your Live Backend via Environment Variable

# In .env (create by copying .env.example)
PUBLIC_API_BASE_URL=https://api.yourrestaurant.com/api/v1

Complete Mapping Table: Website Section → API Endpoint

Website Section        | API Endpoint          | Astro Service Function  | Static Fallback File
-----------------------|-----------------------|-------------------------|--------------------------
Hero Content           | GET  /hero            | getHeroData()           | RESTAURANT_INFO
Menu Categories        | GET  /menu-categories | getMenuCategories()     | MENU_CATEGORIES
Dishes (List & Filter) | GET  /menu?category=  | getMenu(category)       | FULL_MENU
Dish Detail Page       | GET  /menu/{slug}     | getMenuItemBySlug(slug) | FULL_MENU.find(...)
Seasonal Harvest       | GET  /seasonal-harvest| getSeasonalHarvest()    | SEASONAL_HARVEST
Why Dine Reasons       | GET  /why-dine        | getWhyDineReasons()     | WHY_DINE_REASONS
Why Dine Detail Page   | GET  /why-dine/{slug} | getWhyDineBySlug(slug)  | WHY_DINE_REASONS.find(...)
Artisans Profiles      | GET  /artisans        | getArtisans()           | ARTISANS
Artisan Detail Page    | GET  /artisans/{slug} | getArtisanBySlug(slug)  | ARTISANS.find(...)
Guest Reviews          | GET  /reviews         | getReviews()            | REVIEWS
Table Reservation Form | POST /reservations    | createReservation(data) | Simulated Booking Preview
Contact Message Form   | POST /contact         | sendContactMessage(data)| Simulated Message Preview
Newsletter Signup Form | POST /newsletter      | joinNewsletter(data)    | Simulated Signup Preview
Section 5

5. Laravel 11/12 REST Backend Integration Guide

Below is the complete, tested Laravel pipeline covering database migrations, Eloquent models, form request validation, API Resources, and route registration for all restaurant endpoints.

Step 1: Database Migration (All Tables)

// database/migrations/2025_01_01_000000_create_restaurant_tables.php
use Illuminate\Database\Migrations\Migration;
use Illuminate\Database\Schema\Blueprint;
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\Schema;

return new class extends Migration {

        Schema::create('dishes', function (Blueprint $table) {
            $table->id();
            $table->string('slug')->unique();
            $table->string('name');
            $table->enum('category', ['starters', 'mains', 'seasonal', 'desserts', 'drinks', 'brunch']);
            $table->decimal('price', 8, 2);
            $table->text('short_description');
            $table->longText('long_description');
            $table->json('dietary'); // ['GF', 'VG', 'CHEF']
            $table->json('ingredients');
            $table->json('allergens');
            $table->string('cooking_method');
            $table->string('pairing')->nullable();
            $table->string('nutrition_note')->nullable();
            $table->string('image');
            $table->json('gallery')->nullable();
            $table->boolean('highlight')->default(false);
            $table->boolean('seasonal')->default(false);
            $table->boolean('chef_pick')->default(false);
            $table->timestamps();
        });

        // 2. Reservations table
        Schema::create('reservations', function (Blueprint $table) {
            $table->id();
            $table->string('confirmation_code')->unique();
            $table->string('name');
            $table->string('email');
            $table->string('phone');
            $table->date('date');
            $table->string('time');
            $table->integer('guests');
            $table->enum('seating', ['main', 'counter', 'patio', 'private']);
            $table->text('notes')->nullable();
            $table->enum('status', ['confirmed', 'pending', 'cancelled'])->default('confirmed');
            $table->timestamps();
        });

        // 3. Contact Messages table
        Schema::create('contact_messages', function (Blueprint $table) {
            $table->id();
            $table->string('name');
            $table->string('email');
            $table->string('phone')->nullable();
            $table->string('subject');
            $table->text('message');
            $table->timestamps();
        });

        // 4. Newsletter Subscribers table
        Schema::create('newsletter_subscribers', function (Blueprint $table) {
            $table->id();
            $table->string('email')->unique();
            $table->json('preferences')->nullable();
            $table->timestamps();
        });
    }

    public function down(): void {
        Schema::dropIfExists('newsletter_subscribers');
        Schema::dropIfExists('contact_messages');
        Schema::dropIfExists('reservations');
        Schema::dropIfExists('dishes');
    }
};

Step 2: Table Reservation Store Controller

// app/Http/Controllers/Api/V1/ReservationController.php
namespace App\Http\Controllers\Api\V1;

use App\Http\Controllers\Controller;
use App\Models\Reservation;
use Illuminate\Http\Request;
use Illuminate\Support\Str;

class ReservationController extends Controller {
    public function store(Request $request) {
        $validated = $request->validate([
            'name' => 'required|string|max:100',
            'email' => 'required|email|max:150',
            'phone' => 'required|string|max:30',
            'date' => 'required|date|after_or_equal:today',
            'time' => 'required|string',
            'guests' => 'required|integer|min:1|max:20',
            'seating' => 'required|in:main,counter,patio,private',
            'notes' => 'nullable|string|max:500'
        ]);

        $code = 'VH-' . strtoupper(Str::random(6));

        $reservation = Reservation::create([
            ...$validated,
            'confirmation_code' => $code,
            'status' => 'confirmed'
        ]);

        return response()->json([
            'success' => true,
            'confirmationCode' => $code,
            'message' => 'Table reservation confirmed successfully.',
            'reservation' => $reservation
        ], 201);
    }
}

Step 3: Dish API Resource (Formats JSON to Match Astro TypeScript Types)

// app/Http/Resources/DishResource.php
namespace App\Http\Resources;

use Illuminate\Http\Request;
use Illuminate\Http\Resources\Json\JsonResource;

class DishResource extends JsonResource {
    public function toArray(Request $request): array {
        return [
            'id' => (string) $this->id,
            'slug' => $this->slug,
            'name' => $this->name,
            'category' => $this->category,
            'price' => (float) $this->price,
            'shortDescription' => $this->short_description,
            'longDescription' => $this->long_description,
            'dietary' => $this->dietary,
            'ingredients' => $this->ingredients,
            'allergens' => $this->allergens,
            'cookingMethod' => $this->cooking_method,
            'pairing' => $this->pairing,
            'nutritionNote' => $this->nutrition_note,
            'image' => $this->image,
            'gallery' => $this->gallery ?? [],
            'highlight' => (bool) $this->highlight,
            'seasonal' => (bool) $this->seasonal,
            'chefPick' => (bool) $this->chef_pick
        ];
    }
}

Step 4: Dish Query Controller (List & Detail by Slug)

// app/Http/Controllers/Api/V1/DishController.php
namespace App\Http\Controllers\Api\V1;

use App\Http\Controllers\Controller;
use App\Models\Dish;
use App\Http\Resources\DishResource;
use Illuminate\Http\Request;

class DishController extends Controller {
    public function index(Request $request) {
        $query = Dish::query();
        if ($request->has('category')) {
            $query->where('category', $request->query('category'));
        }
        return DishResource::collection($query->get());
    }

    public function show(string $slug) {
        $dish = Dish::where('slug', $slug)->firstOrFail();
        return new DishResource($dish);
    }
}

Step 5: API Routes Registration (routes/api.php)

// routes/api.php
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\Route;
use App\Http\Controllers\Api\V1\DishController;
use App\Http\Controllers\Api\V1\ReservationController;
use App\Http\Controllers\Api\V1\ContactController;
use App\Http\Controllers\Api\V1\NewsletterController;

Route::prefix('v1')->group(function () {
    Route::get('/menu', [DishController::class, 'index']);
    Route::get('/menu/{slug}', [DishController::class, 'show']);
    Route::post('/reservations', [ReservationController::class, 'store']);
    Route::post('/contact', [ContactController::class, 'store']);
    Route::post('/newsletter', [NewsletterController::class, 'store']);
});
CORS Configuration:

In your Laravel config/cors.php, ensure 'paths' => ['api/*', 'sanctum/csrf-cookie'] and 'allowed_origins' => ['http://localhost:4321', 'https://yourdomain.com'] are configured to allow browser preflight requests.

Section 6

6. Next.js (App Router) & Prisma Backend Guide

If your backend is built on Next.js with the App Router, use Prisma ORM and Route Handlers (app/api/v1/.../route.ts):

Step 1: Prisma Schema

// prisma/schema.prisma
datasource db {
  provider = "postgresql"
  url      = env("DATABASE_URL")
}

generator client {
  provider = "prisma-client-js"
}

model Dish {
  id               String   @id @default(cuid())
  slug             String   @unique
  name             String
  category         String   // starters, mains, seasonal, desserts, drinks, brunch
  price            Float
  shortDescription String
  longDescription  String
  dietary          String[]
  ingredients      String[]
  allergens        String[]
  cookingMethod    String
  pairing          String?
  nutritionNote    String?
  image            String
  gallery          String[]
  highlight        Boolean  @default(false)
  seasonal         Boolean  @default(false)
  chefPick         Boolean  @default(false)
  createdAt        DateTime @default(now())
}

model Reservation {
  id               String   @id @default(cuid())
  confirmationCode String   @unique
  name             String
  email            String
  phone            String
  date             DateTime
  time             String
  guests           Int
  seating          String
  notes            String?
  status           String   @default("confirmed")
  createdAt        DateTime @default(now())
}

Step 2: Reservation Route Handler (app/api/v1/reservations/route.ts)

// app/api/v1/reservations/route.ts
import { NextResponse } from 'next/server';
import { prisma } from '@/lib/prisma';

export async function POST(request: Request) {
  try {
    const body = await request.json();
    const { name, email, phone, date, time, guests, seating, notes } = body;

    if (!name || !email || !phone || !date || !time || !guests || !seating) {
      return NextResponse.json(
        { message: 'Validation failed', errors: { form: ['All required fields must be supplied.'] } },
        { status: 422 }
      );
    }

    const confirmationCode = 'VH-' + Math.floor(100000 + Math.random() * 900000);

    const reservation = await prisma.reservation.create({
      data: {
        confirmationCode,
        name,
        email,
        phone,
        date: new Date(date),
        time,
        guests: parseInt(guests, 10),
        seating,
        notes: notes || null
      }
    });

    return NextResponse.json({
      success: true,
      confirmationCode,
      message: 'Reservation created successfully.',
      reservation
    }, { status: 201 });
  } catch (error) {
    return NextResponse.json({ message: 'Internal server error' }, { status: 500 });
  }
}
Section 7

7. Theming, Single Font & Motion Architecture

Self-Hosted Single Font

In strict conformance with template marketplace standards, Verdant Hearth uses one single font family (Plus Jakarta Sans) across headings, body, buttons, navigation, and documentation. Typography hierarchy is achieved through weight (from 400 to 800) and letter-spacing, eliminating dual-font visual clutter. 

/* In src/styles/global.css - Single Font System Across Entire Website */
@import "@fontsource-variable/plus-jakarta-sans";
@import "tailwindcss";

@theme {
  /* One single font family for headings, body, buttons, and navigation */
  --font-sans: 'Plus Jakarta Sans Variable', system-ui, -apple-system, sans-serif;
  --font-serif: 'Plus Jakarta Sans Variable', system-ui, -apple-system, sans-serif;
}

Reduced Motion & Accessibility

All CSS transitions and JavaScript intervals respect the user's operating system preferences. Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, rotation loops and parallax floating are cleanly disabled, ensuring all content remains instantly visible and accessible.

Section 8

8. Troubleshooting & Frequently Asked Questions

Q: Why do forms work even when no API is configured?

This is by design. In static demo mode (when PUBLIC_API_BASE_URL is empty), all forms gracefully simulate successful submissions and generate confirmation codes so commercial buyers can test the complete user experience out of the box.

Q: I get a CORS error when submitting reservations from localhost.

Ensure your backend includes http://localhost:4321 in its allowed CORS origins (e.g., in Laravel's config/cors.php or Next.js CORS headers).

Q: How do I change the website accent colors?

Open src/styles/global.css and update the CSS variables --accent-gold, --brand-forest, and --accent-sage. Both light and dark theme palettes will adapt automatically.
